name: Claude Agent SDK
desc: Anthropic's SDK for building agents on the Claude Code agent loop (tools, sub-agents, MCP); published to PyPI as claude-agent-sdk. Traction: ~8.3k GitHub stars
deployment: searched not found

name: Cline (framework)
desc: Open-source autonomous coding agent shipped as a VS Code/JetBrains extension, CLI (headless for CI) and Node SDK (@cline/sdk) — file edits, terminal, browser, MCP tools.
deployment: Self-hosted only — local IDE extension / CLI / SDK with bring-your-own model keys

name: Composio
desc: Authentication and tool-execution platform for AI agents — 100+ apps with OAuth handled, function-call schemas, observability.
deployment: Managed-only — hosted API + MCP endpoints (Helm charts published for Kubernetes deploys)

name: CrewAI
desc: Multi-agent framework — Crews (sequential) + Flows (event-driven). Open-source core + CrewAI Enterprise. Memory available via Mem0 / Letta adapters (CrewAI Memory cross-listed).
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — OSS library; CrewAI AMP on CrewAI cloud, your VPC or own infra
pricing: free (OSS); AMP Basic free (50 workflow executions/mo); Enterprise custom

name: DSPy
desc: Stanford's framework for programming, not prompting, language models: declarative modules and optimizers for prompts and weights. Traction: ~36.7k GitHub stars
deployment: searched not found

name: Dify
desc: Open-source platform to build agentic workflows and RAG pipelines in a visual, collaborative workspace; self-hosted or Dify Cloud. Traction: ~152k GitHub stars
deployment: searched not found
license: Dify Open Source License (Apache-2.0 based, with additional conditions)

name: Eliza (ai16z)
desc: ai16z's TypeScript agent framework popularised in the crypto/Web3 agent space — multi-platform (Discord, X, Telegram). Brand evolved into elizaOS.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — open-source runtime runs locally; hosted Eliza Cloud (cloud.eliza.app)

name: GPT Engineer
desc: One of the original 'agent writes a whole codebase from a prompt' CLI experiments; precursor to the commercial Lovable (lovable.dev / gptengineer.app). Repository archived (read-only) on 2026-04-22.
deployment: Self-hosted only — CLI

name: Genkit
desc: Google Firebase's open-source framework for building AI-powered applications, with libraries for Node.js and Go (Go in alpha).
deployment: searched not found

name: Google Agent Development Kit (ADK)
desc: Google's code-first Python toolkit for building, evaluating and deploying AI agents. Traction: ~21.1k GitHub stars
deployment: searched not found

name: Haystack (framework)
desc: deepset's open-source framework for LLM/RAG/agent apps — Pipelines abstraction; deepset Cloud commercial. Memory is a downstream connector.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — OSS library; deepset Haystack Enterprise Platform (cloud or custom deployment)
pricing: OSS framework free; Haystack Enterprise Platform: Studio $0 (1 user, 100 pipeline hours, cloud deployment), Enterprise custom

name: Inngest
desc: Event-driven durable workflow platform — competes with Temporal for the JS/TS/Python crowd. Inngest AgentKit (memory cross-listed) is the agent extension.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — Inngest Cloud; self-hosting supported since the 1.0 release
license: SSPL-1.0 with delayed Apache-2.0 grant (server; each release becomes Apache-2.0

name: LangChain (framework)
desc: Dominant Python/JS framework for LLM apps — tool calling, agents, retrievers, runnables. Memory is one component (LangMem cross-listed); the framework itself is the product.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — OSS library; agents deploy to LangSmith Deployment (cloud, hybrid or self-hosted)

name: LangGraph (orchestration)
desc: LangChain's stateful graph runtime for agents — explicit state, persistence, time-travel debugging, human-in-the-loop. Memory is one persistence target (LangGraph Persistence cross-listed).
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — OSS library; LangSmith Deployment cloud, hybrid, or self-hosted Agent Server

name: Langflow
desc: Visual low-code tool for building and deploying AI agents and workflows, with a Python runtime and API/MCP serving. Traction: ~156k GitHub stars
deployment: searched not found

name: LlamaIndex (framework)
desc: Data framework for LLM apps — connectors, indices, query engines, agents, workflows. Memory is one of many subsystems (LlamaIndex Memory cross-listed).
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — OSS library; LlamaAgents workflows deploy to LlamaCloud or self-host

name: MCP Servers (Reference)
desc: Official collection of reference Model Context Protocol servers maintained by the MCP project — currently Everything, Fetch, Filesystem, Git, Memory, Sequential Thinking and Time; earlier servers such as GitHub, Google Drive and PostgreSQL were moved to the servers-archived repo. Substrate for the MCP-memory ecosystem.
deployment: Self-hosted only — run locally via npx (TypeScript) or uvx/pip (Python)
license: Apache-2.0 (transitioning from MIT; contributions without relicensing consent re

name: Magnetic-One
desc: Microsoft Research's generalist multi-agent system — Orchestrator + WebSurfer/FileSurfer/Coder/ComputerTerminal specialists. Built on AutoGen v0.4.
deployment: Self-hosted only — library (autogen-agentchat / autogen-ext)

name: Marvin
desc: Prefect's Python framework for structured outputs (cast, classify, extract, generate) and agentic workflows (tasks, agents, threads). Marvin 3.0 merged in ControlFlow's agentic engine, superseding ControlFlow (whose repo was archived 2026-03-19); uses Pydantic AI for LLM providers.
deployment: Self-hosted only — library

name: Mastra
desc: TypeScript-first agent framework — Workflows, Agents, RAG, eval. Built by the Gatsby team. YC W25.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — Apache-2.0 framework self-hosted; Mastra Platform hosted deployments
pricing: Framework free (Apache-2.0); Mastra Platform Starter $0/mo (100K observability events, 24 CPU hours), Teams $250/mo (1M events, 250 CPU hours, SSO), Enterprise
license: Apache-2.0 (code under ee/ directories under a separate Mastra enterprise licens

name: MetaGPT
desc: Multi-agent framework simulating a software company (PM, Architect, Engineer, QA). Famous for its software-development-via-multi-agent demo.
deployment: Self-hosted only — library

name: Microsoft Agent Framework
desc: Microsoft's framework for building, orchestrating and deploying AI agents and multi-agent workflows in Python and .NET; the successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen. Traction: ~12.6k GitHub stars
deployment: searched not found

name: Microsoft Semantic Kernel
desc: Microsoft's enterprise-focused agent framework — multi-language (C#, Python, Java); Plugins / Planners / Memory; integrates with Azure AI / Foundry. Its README now names Microsoft Agent Framework as the successor; Semantic Kernel still ships releases (maintenance mode).
deployment: Self-hosted only — library

name: Model Context Protocol (MCP spec)
desc: Anthropic-introduced open protocol (Nov 2024) for connecting LLMs to data sources and tools. Donated by Anthropic to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (announced 2025-12-09); now governed as Model Context Protocol, a Series of LF Projects, LLC. Supported across Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, Cursor and many other clients.
deployment: searched not found
license: Apache-2.0 (new spec and code contributions; transitioning from MIT, un-relicens

name: OpenAI Agents SDK
desc: OpenAI's official Python framework for agents — handoffs, guardrails, tracing built in. Successor to OpenAI Swarm (experimental); officially supported.
deployment: Self-hosted only — library

name: OpenAI Swarm (deprecated)
desc: OpenAI Swarm — experimental educational multi-agent framework released Oct 2024; deprecated in favour of the OpenAI Agents SDK in Mar 2025.
deployment: Self-hosted only — library

name: OpenDevin / OpenHands
desc: Open-source SWE agent platform (renamed from OpenDevin to OpenHands). All Hands AI raised $5M; widely used as the OSS counterpart to Devin.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — self-hosted Agent Canvas (free) / Teams, plus OpenHands Cloud and Enterprise
pricing: Agent Canvas free to self-host (BYO LLM key); Teams USD 499/mo for up to 10 users (+USD 50/seat); Enterprise custom

name: Phidata (now Agno)
desc: Multi-modal agent framework (renamed from Phidata to Agno in 2025) — agents, memory, knowledge, tools; emphasis on multi-modal pipelines.
deployment: Self-hosted only — open-source SDK and AgentOS run in your own cloud; paid tiers add a hosted control plane
pricing: Free (control plane against local AgentOS); Pro USD 150/mo (one live AgentOS connection, 3 seats); Enterprise custom

name: Pydantic-AI
desc: Pydantic team's agent framework — type-safe agent definitions, structured outputs, tool calls validated by Pydantic schemas.
deployment: Self-hosted only — library

name: Restate
desc: Durable-execution platform from ex-Confluent / Flink team — Restate Cloud + OSS server; emphasises low-latency invocation vs Temporal's polling.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — Restate Cloud or self-hosted server

name: Strands Agents (AWS)
desc: AWS-released open-source agent SDK, announced 2025-05-16; model-driven approach in which the model plans next steps and tool use. AWS teams including Amazon Q Developer, AWS Glue and VPC Reachability Analyzer use it in production.
deployment: Self-hosted only — library

name: Temporal
desc: Durable-execution platform — Workflows-as-code with crash safety. Used as agent-orchestration backbone at Stripe, Snap, Coinbase, OpenAI Stargate.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — Temporal Cloud or self-hosted Temporal server
pricing: Temporal Cloud: Pay-As-You-Go from USD 50 per million actions (volume down to USD 25/M) plus storage; Business from USD 500/mo; Enterprise and Mission Critical

name: Trigger.dev
desc: Open-source JS/TS background-jobs platform — long-running, retries, observability. Trigger.dev v3 (2024) added 'tasks' abstraction for agent workflows.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — Trigger.dev Cloud or self-hosted (Apache-2.0)
pricing: Free USD 0/mo; Hobby USD 10/mo; Pro USD 50/mo; Enterprise custom

name: Vercel AI SDK
desc: Vercel's TypeScript LLM SDK — streaming, tool calls, structured outputs, agents. Dominant framework for Next.js LLM apps.
deployment: Self-hosted only — library

name: n8n (AI agent flows)
desc: Open-source workflow automation platform with first-class AI Agent / LangChain / Memory / Tool nodes — fastest-growing workflow tool in the AI era.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — n8n Cloud (Starter/Pro/Enterprise) or self-hosted Community/Business editions
pricing: Cloud Starter EUR 20/mo and Pro EUR 50/mo (billed annually); Business EUR 667/mo (self-hosted, billed annually); Enterprise custom; Community Edition self-hoste

name: smolagents (Hugging Face)
desc: Hugging Face's minimal agent library — emphasises code-execution agents (agent writes Python, runs it) over JSON tool-calling. Library is intentionally ~1k LOC.
deployment: Self-hosted only — library

name: Browser Use
desc: Python library that turns any LLM into a browser agent — extracts DOM into a structured representation the LLM can act on (rather than pure screenshot). Browser Use Inc. raised $17M seed Q1 2025 (Felicis); cloud product at cloud.browser-use.com. Project is one of the most-starred browser-agent OSS repos (~60k stars).
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — OSS Python library + Browser Use Cloud; on-prem via sales
pricing: OSS library free; Cloud pay-as-you-go: $1 free credit, $5 min top-up, browsers $0.02/hr, agents = model price +20%; on-prem via sales

name: Bytebot
desc: Open-source desktop-agent runtime that runs an LLM-controlled Linux desktop inside Docker — uses xdotool / X11 capture for control. Pitched as the 'self-hosted Operator' alternative; agent sees a real desktop screen, not just a browser.
deployment: Self-hosted only — Docker (Linux desktop container); repo archived
pricing: Free (Apache-2.0 OSS; repo archived, no paid tier listed)
type: OSS desktop-control agent runtime (containerised Linux desktop)

name: Claude for Chrome
desc: Anthropic's Chrome extension (Claude in Chrome) letting Claude act inside the user's own browser. Research preview Aug 2025; beta for all Max users Nov 2025; on all paid plans since Dec 2025. Distinct from the Computer Use API.
deployment: Managed-only — Chrome extension in the user's browser; model runs in Anthropic cloud
pricing: Not on Free; included in Pro ($20/mo, $17 annual), Max (from $100/mo), Team and Enterprise

name: Highlight AI
desc: Always-on desktop AI assistant that watches the user's screen (across all apps) and answers questions / takes actions based on what's currently visible. Mac + Windows. Founded by Mac Bishop (ex-Mixpanel); raised $13M Series A from Aspect / Lightspeed (Oct 2024). Distinguishes itself from Rewind by being action-oriented (not just recall).
deployment: Desktop app (Mac + Windows); local + cloud hybrid
type: Desktop AI co-pilot (always-on context capture across apps)

name: Hyperbrowser
desc: Cloud-hosted headless browser API tuned for AI agents — captcha solving, stealth mode, session recordings. Y Combinator S24; pitched as a faster / cheaper Browserbase alternative. Used as substrate by agents that need browser execution but don't want to run their own Chromium fleet.
deployment: Cloud only (no self-host)
type: Cloud browser-infrastructure for AI agents (Browserbase competitor)

name: Lutra AI
desc: AI agent platform that automated SaaS workflows across Gmail, Slack, Sheets, etc. using natural-language instructions compiled into durable playbooks. Founded by ex-Google/Facebook engineers; raised seed funding 2024. Discontinued: lutra.ai now states support for Lutra has been discontinued (seen 2026-10-27).
deployment: Cloud only
type: AI agent platform for SaaS automations (Gmail/Slack/Sheets)

name: Magnitude
desc: Formerly an OSS AI browser-agent / natural-language E2E testing framework (YC 2025). The magnitudedev/magnitude repo now hosts an OSS local inference engine + desktop app that serves open models to agents.
deployment: Self-hosted only — local library/desktop app
pricing: OSS free; cloud / enterprise on roadmap
type: OSS browser-agent framework for web tests (YC)

name: OpenAI Operator
desc: OpenAI's general-purpose browser agent — research preview launched January 2025 (US Pro tier). Built on the Computer-Using Agent (CUA) model that processes screenshots and emits mouse / keyboard actions; runs inside an OpenAI-hosted browser sandbox. Operator is the consumer product; the underlying CUA model is the substrate.
deployment: Cloud (OpenAI-hosted browser sandbox) — no self-host

name: Project Mariner
desc: Google DeepMind's experimental browser agent built on Gemini 2.0, a Chrome extension that took actions on the user's behalf. Research preview launched Dec 2024 as Google's answer to OpenAI Operator / Anthropic Computer Use. Shut down on 2026-05-04; Google directs users to Gemini for complex agentic tasks.
deployment: Chrome extension + Google Cloud

name: Skyvern
desc: Open-source autonomous browser agent that uses computer vision + LLMs to navigate websites. Workflow-based: agents follow recorded plans that adapt to layout changes. Skyvern Inc. raised $4.5M seed (Sep-2024, Felicis lead). Self-hostable; cloud version on skyvern.com.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — Docker/pip self-host + Skyvern Cloud (cloud anti-bot features not in OSS)

name: Stagehand
desc: Open-source browser-automation framework by Browserbase (TypeScript core plus Python and Go SDKs). Mixes Playwright-style code with natural-language act/extract/observe; pairs with Browserbase Cloud.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — library runs locally; Browserbase cloud browsers optional
pricing: OSS free; Browserbase Cloud handles runtime

name: Steel.dev
desc: Open-source browser API ('the browser for agents') — Chromium fleet with stealth mode, session recordings, CDP. OSS repo + managed cloud. Compatible with Playwright / Puppeteer. Distinguishes itself as the 'OSS Browserbase'.
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — Docker self-host (steel-browser) + Steel Cloud
type: OSS + cloud browser-infrastructure for AI agents

name: UI-TARS
desc: ByteDance Seed's open-source GUI-agent foundation model — released Jan 2025; trained end-to-end on screenshot → action pairs. Comes with UI-TARS-Desktop (Electron app) that runs the model against the user's screen. SOTA on OSWorld at release; weights on HuggingFace.
deployment: Self-hosted only — open weights (Hugging Face) + UI-TARS-desktop / Agent TARS app
type: OSS GUI-agent foundation model + desktop app (ByteDance)

name: Adept ACT
desc: Founded 2022 by David Luan and fellow ex-OpenAI / Google researchers. Built ACT-1 / ACT-2 multimodal action transformers for computer-use. In June 2024 Amazon hired Luan and co-founders (Odena, Nye, Elsen, Szot) into Amazon AGI and licensed Adept's technology (acqui-hire, not a full acquisition); Adept continues with former head of engineering Zach Brock as CEO, refocused on agentic AI solutions.
deployment: not applicable — orchestration platform, not memory product
type: Computer-use / workflow-automation agent (Adept now part of Amazon AGI 2024)

name: CrewAI Enterprise
desc: Commercial Enterprise tier of the CrewAI OSS multi-agent framework. Adds managed cloud runtime, RBAC, audit logging, SLA support, on-prem option. OSS CrewAI is in the Framework-embedded memory section already; this row covers the commercial cloud platform separately. $18M Series A Oct-2024 (Insight Partners). 30k+ companies have deployed CrewAI agents in prod (vendor-stated).
deployment: Both (self-hosted + managed cloud) — CrewAI cloud, dedicated VPC or your own infrastructure (Enterprise)
pricing: Basic free (50 workflow executions/mo, 2 automations); Enterprise custom — no public self-serve paid tier
type: Commercial multi-agent orchestration platform (vs OSS CrewAI)

name: Imbue (formerly Generally Intelligent)
desc: Founded 2017 as Generally Intelligent; rebranded Imbue 2023. Founders Kanjun Qiu + Josh Albrecht. $200M Series B 2023 ($1B valuation). Trained a 70B reasoning model, then shifted to user-owned AI tools: imbue.com now lists Studio (personal AI operating system, waitlist), Bouncer, Cloud in a Bottle, Sculptor, Vet (AI code review) and mngr (CLI for managing coding agents), with open-source repos und
deployment: not applicable — orchestration platform, not memory product
type: Coding-agent research lab (foundation models for reasoning + code agents)

name: InstructLab (Red Hat / IBM)
desc: Red Hat / IBM-stewarded open-source framework for community-driven LLM alignment + fine-tuning (LAB method, IBM Research 2024; Granite models). Apache 2.0. Main CLI repo archived 2026-04-23 after a 2025 refactor into separate libraries — synthetic data generation in SDG Hub and training in Training Hub (Red-Hat-AI-Innovation-Team). Not strictly a multi-agent framework.
deployment: Self-hosted only — CLI/library (archived)
pricing: OSS (free); IBM watsonx + Red Hat OpenShift AI commercial pricing for the platforms
type: OSS LLM alignment + community-driven fine-tuning framework

name: Lindy
desc: Lindy is a no-code multi-agent automation platform from Florent Crivello (ex-Teleport, ex-Twitter). Targets consumer / SMB segment with email triage, meeting scheduling, CRM-update agents. $50M Series A Oct-2024 led by Andreessen Horowitz + Sequoia. Distinct from Zapier / n8n traditional automation by putting LLMs at the core of every workflow node.
deployment: Managed cloud (SaaS only)
pricing: Free: $50 in credits for 7 days, no card; Team $29.99/user/mo (3,000 credits, extra $10 per 1,000); Enterprise custom
type: No-code commercial multi-agent automation platform (consumer / SMB)
